belief: What other people think of me is what matters most.
origins: In close communities, reputation can feel like survival. Gossip, church talk, and neighborhood watchfulness teach us to monitor how we look to others. Social media has widened that audience. We learn to adjust ourselves to be accepted and fear being talked about.
teaches: Paul asks, “Am I now seeking the approval of men, or of God?” Proverbs says, “The fear of man is a snare, but whoever trusts in the LORD is set securely on high.” God told Samuel, “Man sees the outward appearance, but the LORD sees the heart.” Jesus warned about doing good “to be seen by men.” Proverbs adds that “a good name is more desirable than great riches,” which means character matters, but it is built by integrity, not by managing impressions. The final opinion that matters is God’s.
self_statements: If people think badly of me, I am ruined.
I have to manage how I come across.
I cannot stand being talked about.
errors: Assuming I know what others think.
Believing everyone is watching and judging me.
Insisting that I must always be approved.
Feeling exposed and concluding that I am judged.
questions: Whose opinion do I fear most, and why?
What have I done to win approval that did not feel like me?
What does a good name actually rest on?
What does Scripture say about the fear of man?
What would change if I cared most about God’s view?
What is one place I can be more honest?
truth: A good name is built by integrity, not by managing impressions. The fear of man is a snare, and God’s view of me is what matters most. I can live honestly and let my character speak.
hw_truths: The fear of man is a snare.
A good name comes from integrity.
I do not have to please everyone.
The Lord is on my side.
log: Each week, note one time you chose honesty over impression.
actions: Write whose opinions you fear most.
Note what people actually say or do.
Do one thing because it is right, not because it is seen.
Say it before a hard moment.
prayer: Lord, I have lived under the weight of others’ opinions. Free me from the fear of man, and let me live honestly before You. Amen.
hw_questions: What do I do to win approval?
What does a good name rest on?
name_example: Sarah can write: “I trust the Lord, so I am set securely on high.”
